findings.body: The accepted amount grammar permits leading zeroes, and normalization only pads the decimal places. A valid operand such as `000500000` therefore reaches this formatter as `000500000.00` and is rendered in the new chip/readback as `₹00,05,00,000` instead of `₹5,00,000`. Strip leading zeroes while preserving zero before applying Indian grouping.
findings.title: Canonicalize leading zeroes before formatting comparison amounts

findings.body: Selecting the first domain with any money measure can omit the figure-to-figure example even when the user can perform one. For example, a user permitted only Actual in `governed-financial` but Actual and Budget in `mis-statement` gets only the amount example because the first domain's one-element array wins. Select a domain with at least two permitted money measures for the binary example, independently of the domain used for the amount example.
findings.title: Choose a domain with two measures for the binary help example
